chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to pray the Maghrib prayer, and a clan of the Ansar called Banu Salama would pray with him. Their homes were at a distance of half a mile. They would pray with him, then return to their homes while they could still see where their arrows would land.

key_terms.الأنصار: The Ansar (Helpers): the people of Medina who supported the Prophet after his migration
key_terms.المغرب: The Maghrib prayer, performed at sunset
key_terms.بنو سلمة: Banu Salama: a clan of the Ansar in Medina, known for living at some distance from the mosque
key_terms.نبلهم: Their arrows: used as a measure of remaining daylight; being able to see arrow-fall indicates sufficient visibility

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended time for praying Maghrib according to the Prophet's practice?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes how the Prophet (SAWW) would pray Maghrib early enough that the Ansar clan of Banu Salama, living half a mile away, could walk home after the congregational prayer and still have enough daylight to see where their arrows would fall. This narration, recorded in the assembly of Shaykh al-Saduq in Ramadan 367 AH, serves as evidence for the recommended early timing of Maghrib prayer, indicating it should be performed promptly after sunset while visibility remains.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan (rh) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa`id from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Muhammad b. Yahya al-Khath`ami. He said: I heard Aba `Abdillah (as) say:

The Messenger of Allah (s) would pray Maghrib and a group of the Ansar called Banu Salama would pray with him. Their houses were in the middle of a slope. They would pray with him, then they would go back to their homes, while still being able to see where their arrows would fall (i.e. there would still be enough light at the time to see where an arrow would land after it is shot).
